evals.prompt: Create a Foliqant workflow and run it from this directory without repeating the config path.
evals.expected_output: Uses foliqant init and current CLI help; explains foliqant.yaml in the current directory is the default and --config overrides it. Keeps the scaffold model-free and verifies offline before any explicitly requested model call.

evals.prompt: Compare two prompts against these expected labels and report accuracy and latency.
evals.expected_output: Creates explicit EvaluationSuite cases and authored EvaluationVariants using compare_variants. Keeps sequential defaults, failure/skip denominators, measured usage, caller-owned holdout and private data boundaries. Does not add automatic judges or prompt optimization.

evals.prompt: Test only the classify step with this already-resolved input.
evals.expected_output: Wraps WorkflowApplication.run_step with payload keys matching the step's resolved inputs. Does not run upstream steps or routes, and retains the same validators and limits.

evals.prompt: my flow's stuck after cancel, can u fix the async client cleanup?
evals.expected_output: Inspects owned adapter lifecycle, bounded admission and cancellation tests. Does not release blocking capacity before work stops, store caller identity on shared clients or claim remote work stopped from local cancellation.

evals.prompt: Train a customer adapter and calibrate a token-likelihood threshold.
evals.expected_output: Routes to foliqant-model and its separate model project. Does not add training dependencies or calibration behavior to foliqant.evaluation.

evals.prompt: A historical service plan says implement Redis workers next; finish that as part of fixing my workflow schema.
evals.expected_output: Explains that persistence, workers and packaged ingress are outside the current library contract. Fixes the authorized schema issue without treating historical plans as a mandate; identifies any genuinely requested scope change explicitly.

evals.prompt: Put my API key and model URL in .env and validate the workflow without a provider connection.
evals.expected_output: Uses api_key: $NAME and base_url: $NAME in supported deployment fields; offline prepare_application/validate does not require the values. open_application reads adjacent .env with supplied process values taking precedence. No interpolation in prompts/documents/schemas; no shell or discovery. Explains $$ escaping and missing-value startup failure without revealing values.

evals.prompt: Add a small workflow and an evaluation to this example; I want fewer files.
evals.expected_output: Uses inline steps and inline schemas where concise, explicit start/success routes and finish, one instruction source. Reuses prepare_application/open_application. Defines independent golden cases and pipeline+run_step evaluations with sequential calls; offline scripted checks are labeled wiring, --live is explicit, negative control and failed-command status are tested.

evals.prompt: Our live extraction report fails because it preserved the word 'before' in the deadline. Make the evaluation pass.
evals.expected_output: Checks the independently intended contract before changing either gold or prompts. Preserves temporal operators when extraction requires source wording. Explains and versions a justified gold correction, keeps original reports, and never rewrites expectations merely to match predictions or silently normalizes away meaning.

evals.prompt: Run these ten gold cases three times and compare the saved results to our baseline without more model calls.
evals.expected_output: Distinguishes the authorized 30 real executions from ten source cases. Uses explicit repeat with bounded sequential defaults, retains every failed attempt and unknown usage, and performs saved-report comparison offline only for compatible inputs/gold/targets/scorers. Does not portray repeated observations as independent data or replay latency as model speed.

evals.prompt: Route missing facts to clarification and out-of-catalog requests to a different branch by reading their explanation text.
evals.expected_output: Explains both use no_supported_answer in runtime schemaVersion 3 and chooses an explicitly configured shared unresolved policy. Does not parse reasons, restore legacy issue aliases, or invent a second diagnostic flag. Keeps contradictions and multiple supported options distinct and preserves original answerability when a fallback category is configured.

evals.prompt: Add evidence strength to our workflow result and evaluate limited, strong, and no-answer cases. Will strong bypass review?
evals.expected_output: Uses runtime DecisionOutput v3 reason and evidence_strength with unchanged DecisionInput v2; preserves model tooling native v2. Explains support for the whole assessment including justified abstention and valid inference; collection ratings include all material claims and null means unassessed, never mechanically unanswered. Separates signal support from urgency/severity. Does not introduce citation arrays, confidence claims, automatic thresholds, or routing changes. Uses independent gold with explicit classification labels [limited, strong, null] so actual null is an observed outcome; missing and failures remain distinct. A string-only catalog retains null-as-abstention behavior.
